# mamba-ascendc

> Native AscendC implementation of the Mamba-2 Structured State Space Duality (SSD) forward and backward operator for Huawei Ascend NPU.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/So-cean/mamba-ascendc
Current release: v0.1.1
Primary language/runtime: AscendC, C++, Python, PyTorch, CANN
License for original code: Apache-2.0

## Core facts

- The primary NPU implementation is a native AscendC custom operator, not a Triton port.
- The repository includes PyTorch reference, Triton-Ascend forward, AscendC forward/backward, and upstream A100 mamba_ssm comparison paths.
- Tested accelerators are Ascend 910B3, Ascend 950PR, and NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe.
- Public tensors are FP32. Cube operations use FP16 operands with FP32 accumulation internally.
- The high-performance M1 backward path currently requires contiguous FP32 tensors and P=N=chunk_size=64.

## Public API

- AscendC: `from ascend_kernel import mamba2_ssd_fwd`
- PyTorch reference: `from mamba_torch import ssd_chunk_scan_ref`
- Triton-Ascend: `from mamba_triton_ascend.mamba2 import mamba_chunk_scan_combined`
- The public tensor semantics follow `mamba_ssm.ops.triton.ssd_combined.mamba_chunk_scan_combined`.

## Performance snapshot

- Heavy forward shape order: B,L,H,P,N,chunk,G.
- Heavy forward shape: [8,4096,256,64,64,64,64].
- Ascend 910B3 AscendC forward median: 31.888 ms.
- NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe upstream mamba_ssm forward median: 22.583 ms.
- Ascend 910B3 relative throughput for this identical workload: 70.82% of A100.
- Timing uses device events, warmup=10, repeat=30, and median latency.
- The repository does not normalize results with vendor theoretical TFLOPS.

## Source entry points

- `mamba_ascendc/`: public API, autograd, Vector/fallback kernels, and PyTorch extension.
- `mamba_ascendc_ops/`: AscendC Cube/MIX custom operator projects.
- `mamba_triton_ascend/mamba2/`: Triton-Ascend forward implementation.
- `mamba_torch/`: mathematical reference and pure Vision-Mamba2 integration.
- `benchmarks/`: A100, Ascend, scaling, and profiler entry points.
- `tests/mamba2/`: reference, GPU, Triton-Ascend, and integration tests.

## Current constraints

- M1 backward supports contiguous FP32 with P=N=chunk_size=64.
- Variable-length and packed sequences are not implemented.
- BF16 and additional N/chunk_size combinations remain roadmap items.
- NPU compilation and msprof reproduction require the documented CANN and device environment.

## External references

- Mamba upstream: https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba
- Mamba-2 paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060
- Triton-Ascend: https://github.com/Ascend/triton-ascend
